how_we_lost: P3 (Y'shtola) killed us on round 10 (turn 38). P3 cast Transpose and then Exsanguinate off 9 lands, Sol Ring, two Talismans and Lyse Hext's cost reduction. Y'shtola pinged 2 per spell, and we went from about 14 to -2 (P2 died in the same turn). On round 9 we had Muldrotha, Braids and a recast Pernicious Deed on board. The memo said to pop the Deed at X=4, which would have killed all eight of P3's creatures (Y'shtola and Lyse Hext included) plus the rocks that paid for Exsanguinate. Instead we cast Hostage Taker on Drivnod, and P2's Plaguecrafter took Taker back the next turn. We had Glen Elendra, and later Swan Song, in hand with no mana open for P3's turn.
winnable_why: Draws were thin (a 2-land keep, and the sixth land only on round 8), and P3 built a large board. But the early misuse of Assassin's Trophy, Animate Dead and Survival cost two rounds of development, and the round 9 Deed skip left P3's kill turn intact. A strong pilot has perhaps a 20-30% game here, not a likely win.

mistakes.what_happened: The round 9 memo: recast Pernicious Deed from the graveyard and pop it at X=4. That kills Y'shtola, both Alphinauds, Alisaie, G'raha, Lyse Hext, the Hero and Wizard tokens, Helm, both Talismans and Sol Ring, while Muldrotha survives. The executor cast the Deed but then accepted Forge's Hostage Taker cast, redirected to Drivnod, and never activated the Deed. Sol Ring stayed in hand (it was only held because the Deed would kill it).
mistakes.better_play: Deed at X=4 as planned (Deed 3 + X 4 = 7 mana), and then Claws. Drivnod doesn't double emblem triggers, since an emblem isn't a permanent, so its threat could wait a turn.
mistakes.why: P3's next turn used exactly that board: Y'shtola pings, Lyse's cost reduction, and Sol Ring plus Talismans for a big Exsanguinate. Without them, P3's Exsanguinate tops out around X=7 with no Y'shtola pings. From 20 life we very likely survive, even after some emblem drains from the Deed deaths (Forge aimed those at P3 all game). The Hostage Taker line gained nothing, because Taker was edicted the next turn.

mistakes.what_happened: Round 3. The memo said to cast Survival and hold Assassin's Trophy for Sephiroth, Altar, Plunderer or Grave Pact, with Animate Dead reserved for Gravebreaker Lamia. Forge cast Trophy in our draw step, and the executor aimed it at P2's Nykthos (a land) rather than Forge's Delney. Animate Dead then reanimated P1's Nazgûl, which died to Claim the Precious the next turn. Survival was not cast.
mistakes.better_play: Play the land, cast Survival, and hold Trophy mana. Sephiroth arrived two turns later, and P3 had to spend Lethal Scheme on it.
mistakes.why: It burned our only instant-speed removal and our Lamia-setup card for nothing, and it delayed the Survival engine by a round.

mistakes.what_happened: On rounds 4 and 5 the memos said to use Survival to fetch Sakura-Tribe Elder, ramping to Muldrotha on round 6. The executor fetched Hostage Taker instead, which was never cast and was discarded the next turn. Next it fetched Plaguecrafter, whose edict hit only P3's 0/1 Wizard token. Soul-Guide Lantern was cast and sacrificed at once, even though the memo said to hold it until Muldrotha. At P3's end step the executor overruled Forge to activate Claws of Gix, which sacrificed itself for 1 life.
mistakes.better_play: Fetch Sakura-Tribe Elder both times and cast it. Muldrotha then lands on round 6 with Lantern and Claws still available.
mistakes.why: Muldrotha slipped from round 6 to round 8, and three cheap permanents that her lanes wanted were thrown away.

mistakes.what_happened: P3 was a known Exsanguinate deck (the dossier says 'counter Exsanguinate') with 13+ mana and Y'shtola out. Even so, the round 9 memo held Glen Elendra 'until we can leave U open' and tapped out for sorcery-speed plays. The escalation memos then listed Swan Song as protection with 0 mana available on P2's and P3's turns.
mistakes.better_play: Treat Exsanguinate as the main threat once P3 had about 13 mana. Cast Glen Elendra (4) and keep {U} up, or leave U open for Swan Song, before chasing Drivnod.
mistakes.why: Exsanguinate was the card that killed us, and we held two answers to it with no mana behind them.

mistakes.what_happened: On round 6 the strategist held Muldrotha, which was castable with 6 mana, because of P2's Dictate of Erebos, and cast Pernicious Deed to pop next turn at X=5. P3's Cleansing Nova (artifact/enchantment mode) destroyed the Deed while we had 3 mana open, and it was never popped in response.
mistakes.better_play: Pop the Deed in response at X=3, killing P2's Soultrader, Alisaie, P1's rocks and tokens, instead of losing it for nothing.
mistakes.why: Our only board reset was lost, along with Survival and Signet, for no value. Holding Muldrotha into Dictate was itself defensible.

strategy_assessment: The memos again ranked P2 (Sephiroth) first and P3's Y'shtola as 'low priority' through round 5, and P3 won. Holding Muldrotha into a Dictate of Erebos plus Skeleton/Soultrader edict loop on round 6 was a reasonable call. The recurring plan (Survival → Lamia → Capsule, Deed resets, Braids drains) was sound but never ran, because the executor spent the early tutors and removal elsewhere. From round 8 the right priority was P3's engine: Y'shtola, Lyse and the mana rocks, which the Deed at X=4 answered. We also needed to hold counter mana against Exsanguinate instead of tapping out for Hostage Taker and Drivnod.
summary: We lost to P3's Transpose plus Exsanguinate on round 10. The early game was squandered: Trophy hit a land, Animate Dead went on a doomed Nazgûl, and Survival fetched Hostage Taker and a Plaguecrafter that edicted a token instead of the ramp creature, so Muldrotha arrived on round 8. On round 9 the executor skipped the memo's Pernicious Deed at X=4, which would have gutted P3's board and mana, and we held Glen Elendra and Swan Song without open mana.
